title: Mlai mid domain embeddings
question: What is an embedding, and why are they useful compared to representing categorical or text data with one-hot encoding?
idealAnswer:
An embedding is a learned, dense, lower-dimensional vector representation of an entity, such as a word, item, user, or category, that captures semantic relationships in the geometry of the vector space

One-hot encoding treats every category as equally different from every other, with no notion of similarity, embeddings place similar entities closer together in the vector space

Embeddings are typically learned jointly with the model on a task, or pretrained separately, like word2vec or transformer embeddings, rather than hand-designed

They dramatically reduce dimensionality compared to one-hot encoding for high-cardinality categories, e.g. millions of user or product IDs, which one-hot encoding handles very poorly

Because they encode similarity, embeddings enable useful operations like nearest-neighbor search, recommendation, and transfer to related tasks
